name: SSC Cloze Connectors and Transition Words
description: Connector and transition word usage for SSC cloze tests, with clue patterns and examples.

cards.definition:
Use: adds a stronger extra point

Cloze clue: Use when the second point strengthens the first.

Example: The plan is cheap. Moreover, it can be finished before the deadline.

Use: adds formal extra information

Cloze clue: Use in essays and reports to add one more serious point.

Example: The library is quiet. Furthermore, it has the exact book everyone wants.

Use: adds another point

Cloze clue: Use when one fact is not enough and another supporting fact follows.

Example: The course is short. In addition, the notes are clear.

Use: also or as an extra point

Cloze clue: Use for formal addition.

Example: The app works offline. Additionally, it syncs when internet returns.

Use: apart from that or in addition

Cloze clue: Use when adding an extra practical reason.

Example: I will not buy the shoes. Besides, my wallet has already fainted.

Use: adds a simple extra point

Cloze clue: Use for common addition in simple sentences.

Example: She revised grammar and also solved mock tests.

Use: in addition to

Cloze clue: Use to connect two related nouns or actions.

Example: He studies vocabulary as well as grammar.

Use: adds two strong linked points

Cloze clue: Use when both points are important and parallel.

Example: She is not only fast but also accurate.

Use: also

Cloze clue: Use at the end of a sentence for simple addition.

Example: He solved the puzzle too.

Use: in the same way

Cloze clue: Use when the second idea is similar to the first.

Example: Good food needs patience. Likewise, good grammar needs practice.

Use: in a similar manner

Cloze clue: Use for comparison between similar ideas.

Example: Delhi has heavy traffic. Similarly, Mumbai has crowded roads.

Use: besides this

Cloze clue: Use when adding one more separate point.

Example: The phone is fast. Apart from this, the battery lasts all day.

Use: combined with

Cloze clue: Use when two factors together create a result.

Example: Hard work coupled with revision improved her score.

Use: together with

Cloze clue: Use to add a companion detail.

Example: He carried his admit card along with two pens.

Use: shows contrast

Cloze clue: Use when the second idea opposes the first.

Example: He knew the rule, but the tricky option fooled him.

Use: shows contrast in a formal way

Cloze clue: Use after a full stop or strong pause in writing.

Example: The shortcut looked easy. However, it failed in the real question.

Use: but or still

Cloze clue: Use for surprising contrast.

Example: The question was short, yet everyone got it wrong.

Use: despite that

Cloze clue: Use when something continues despite a problem.

Example: He was tired. Still, he revised one more chapter.

Use: despite what was just said

Cloze clue: Use for formal contrast after a difficult point.

Example: The road was flooded. Nevertheless, the volunteers reached the village.

Use: nevertheless

Cloze clue: Use in formal writing to show contrast.

Example: The plan was risky. Nonetheless, it worked.

Use: introduces an opposite viewpoint

Cloze clue: Use when comparing two sides.

Example: Online classes save travel time. On the other hand, distractions are everywhere.

Use: shows clear difference

Cloze clue: Use when the second thing is unlike the first.

Example: The first answer was vague. In contrast, the second was precise.

Use: in the opposite way

Cloze clue: Use for logical opposite relationships.

Example: Practice improves speed. Conversely, panic reduces accuracy.

Use: while in contrast

Cloze clue: Use to compare two different facts in one sentence.

Example: Ravi likes theory, whereas Sita prefers examples.

Use: although or whereas

Cloze clue: Use to show contrast between two facts.

Example: While the rule is simple, its exceptions are tricky.

Use: despite the fact that

Cloze clue: Use before a contrast clause.

Example: Although he started late, he finished first.

Use: although

Cloze clue: Use for a lighter contrast.

Example: Though the answer looked odd, it was correct.

Use: stronger although

Cloze clue: Use when the contrast is surprising.

Example: Even though she was tired, she revised the errors.

Use: in spite of

Cloze clue: Use before a noun or gerund, not a full clause.

Example: Despite the rain, the match continued.

Use: despite

Cloze clue: Use before a noun or gerund.

Example: In spite of low marks, she did not quit.

Use: different from

Cloze clue: Use when comparing difference.

Example: Unlike his excuse, the CCTV was reliable.

Use: instead or more accurately

Cloze clue: Use to correct or replace an earlier idea.

Example: The problem is not the syllabus. Rather, it is revision strategy.

Use: as an alternative

Cloze clue: Use when one thing replaces another.

Example: He did not guess. Instead, he eliminated two options.

Use: if not, then a bad result will follow

Cloze clue: Use to show consequence of not doing something.

Example: Read the instructions. Otherwise, easy marks will escape.

Use: despite that

Cloze clue: Use when a surprising result follows.

Example: The price was high. Even so, the shop was crowded.

Use: despite

Cloze clue: Use in formal writing before or after a noun phrase.

Example: Notwithstanding the delay, the project succeeded.

Use: used to deny and state the opposite

Cloze clue: Use when the second statement directly rejects the first.

Example: He is not careless. On the contrary, he checks every detail.

Use: not at all, opposite of

Cloze clue: Use to reject an idea strongly.

Example: Far from being easy, the passage was full of traps.

Use: however, also true

Cloze clue: Use to balance two points.

Example: Speed matters. At the same time, accuracy is vital.

Use: for the reason that

Cloze clue: Use before a cause clause.

Example: He missed the bus because he trusted a five-minute nap.

Use: because or from a time

Cloze clue: Use when the reason is already known or obvious.

Example: Since the road was blocked, we took another route.

Use: because or in the way that

Cloze clue: Use for a reason that is not the main focus.

Example: As it was getting dark, they returned home.

Use: because, formal or literary

Cloze clue: Use after a comma to give a reason.

Example: He stayed silent, for he knew the truth.

Use: because of

Cloze clue: Use before a noun phrase, often after be verb.

Example: The match was delayed due to heavy rain.

Use: as a result of

Cloze clue: Use before a noun or noun phrase.

Example: Because of one missing document, the form was rejected.

Use: because of

Cloze clue: Use formally before a noun phrase.

Example: Owing to fog, the train arrived late.

Use: because of

Cloze clue: Use for formal cause.

Example: The school remained closed on account of heavy rain.

Use: because of, often positive but can be sarcastic

Cloze clue: Use when giving credit or blame.

Example: Thanks to daily revision, she spotted the trap immediately.

Use: considering

Cloze clue: Use for formal reason before a decision.

Example: In view of the storm warning, the event was postponed.

Use: because

Cloze clue: Use when the reason is obvious from the situation.

Example: Seeing that he had no ID card, the guard stopped him.

Use: because now something has happened

Cloze clue: Use when a new situation creates a reason.

Example: Now that the syllabus is over, revision must begin.

Use: considering that

Cloze clue: Use in formal reasoning.

Example: Given that time is short, guessing blindly is dangerous.

Use: taking into account

Cloze clue: Use before a reason or circumstance.

Example: Considering that he began late, his score was impressive.

Use: because of

Cloze clue: Use before a noun phrase showing cause.

Example: As a result of poor planning, the budget collapsed.

Use: for that reason

Cloze clue: Use when the second sentence is a logical result.

Example: The road was flooded. Therefore, the buses were delayed.

Use: therefore or in this way

Cloze clue: Use for formal result or method.

Example: He revised daily. Thus, his accuracy improved.

Use: therefore

Cloze clue: Use for logical conclusion, often concise.

Example: The evidence was weak. Hence, the case failed.

Use: as a result

Cloze clue: Use when one event causes another.

Example: He ignored the warning. Consequently, he lost marks.

Use: therefore

Cloze clue: Use to show outcome.

Example: She practised daily. As a result, her speed improved.

Use: therefore

Cloze clue: Use for simple result.

Example: It was late, so we returned home.

Use: therefore or in a suitable way

Cloze clue: Use when action follows a decision or situation.

Example: The rules changed. Accordingly, the form was updated.

Use: because of this

Cloze clue: Use before a conclusion.

Example: The passage was full of traps. For this reason, slow reading helped.

Use: for that reason

Cloze clue: Use when explaining a result.

Example: He skipped revision. That is why the easy question hurt him.

Use: by that means

Cloze clue: Use when an action produces a result.

Example: She saved small amounts daily, thereby building an emergency fund.

Use: this caused

Cloze clue: Use when one event causes another.

Example: The delay led to confusion at the counter.

Use: this caused

Cloze clue: Use for formal outcome.

Example: Poor drainage resulted in flooding.

Use: in order to

Cloze clue: Use before base verb to show purpose.

Example: She woke early to revise before the house became noisy.

Use: for the purpose of

Cloze clue: Use for clear formal purpose.

Example: He saved money in order to buy a laptop.

Use: in order to

Cloze clue: Use for purpose, usually before a base verb.

Example: She spoke slowly so as to be understood.

Use: in order that

Cloze clue: Use before a full clause showing purpose.

Example: He wrote clearly so that the examiner could read it.

Use: so that, formal

Cloze clue: Use before a clause, often with may or might.

Example: The notice was displayed in order that everyone might see it.

Use: with the aim of

Cloze clue: Use before gerund or noun.

Example: He studied grammar with a view to improving accuracy.

Use: with the aim of

Cloze clue: Use before gerund or noun.

Example: The survey was conducted for the purpose of collecting data.

Use: planning to

Cloze clue: Use before gerund.

Example: She joined the course with the intention of improving English.

Use: so that not

Cloze clue: Use to show prevention of an unwanted result, often with should.

Example: Work carefully lest you should lose easy marks.

Use: because one is afraid that

Cloze clue: Use to show purpose of avoiding danger.

Example: He saved a backup for fear that the file might vanish.

Use: on the condition that

Cloze clue: Use for real or possible condition.

Example: If you read the question twice, half the traps lose power.

Use: if not

Cloze clue: Use for negative condition without adding not.

Example: Unless you revise, the rules will look like strangers.

Use: only if

Cloze clue: Use for a strict condition.

Example: You may enter provided that you carry your admit card.

Use: provided that

Cloze clue: Use for condition, slightly less formal.

Example: You can borrow my notes providing that you return them.

Use: provided that

Cloze clue: Use for condition over a duration or requirement.

Example: You can use my pen as long as it comes back alive.

Use: as long as

Cloze clue: Use for condition.

Example: So long as you practise, improvement is possible.

Use: because something may happen

Cloze clue: Use for precaution, not simply if.

Example: Carry an umbrella in case it rains.

Use: if, formal

Cloze clue: Use in formal conditions.

Example: In the event that the server fails, submit the form offline.

Use: only if

Cloze clue: Use for strict agreement.

Example: He agreed on condition that the work would be shared.

Use: if we accept that

Cloze clue: Use for hypothetical reasoning.

Example: Assuming that the data are correct, the result is alarming.

Use: if

Cloze clue: Use for imagined condition.

Example: Supposing that the train is late, what will you do?

Use: whether or not, despite possibility

Cloze clue: Use for condition that will not change the result.

Example: Even if the paper is tough, stay calm.

Use: under no other condition

Cloze clue: Use for strict condition.

Example: You will improve only if you analyse mistakes.

Use: wish or regret

Cloze clue: Use to express strong wish, not condition for result.

Example: If only I had revised articles earlier.

Use: regardless of whether

Cloze clue: Use when both possibilities lead to same result.

Example: Whether or not he agrees, the rule remains valid.

Use: at the time that

Cloze clue: Use for time relationship.

Example: When the bell rang, everyone suddenly remembered speed.

Use: throughout a period

Cloze clue: Use before a noun phrase, not a full clause.

Example: During the exam, the water bottle became emotionally important.

Use: immediately after

Cloze clue: Use when one action follows another quickly.

Example: As soon as the result appeared, the website slowed down.

Use: earlier than

Cloze clue: Use for earlier time.

Example: Check the answer before you submit.

Use: later than

Cloze clue: Use for later time.

Example: After the rain stopped, the road still looked doubtful.

Use: up to the time when

Cloze clue: Use to show continuation till a point.

Example: Wait until the invigilator gives the signal.

Use: until, less formal

Cloze clue: Use for continuation up to a time.

Example: He studied till midnight and then studied his ceiling.

Use: at the same time

Cloze clue: Use when another event happens during a period.

Example: The forms were being checked. Meanwhile, the candidates guarded their pens.

Use: during the intervening time

Cloze clue: Use for action while waiting.

Example: The bus was delayed. In the meantime, we revised vocabulary.

Use: after that

Cloze clue: Use for formal sequence.

Example: The exam ended. Thereafter, the answer keys were released.

Use: later

Cloze clue: Use for formal later event.

Example: The rule was changed. Subsequently, new forms were issued.

Use: earlier

Cloze clue: Use when referring to earlier time.

Example: Previously, the office accepted handwritten forms.

Use: before this time

Cloze clue: Use for a past point.

Example: Earlier, he had ignored the same warning.

Use: after some time

Cloze clue: Use for a following event.

Example: Later, the simple-looking clue became important.

Use: in the end

Cloze clue: Use for final result after time or effort.

Example: Eventually, the lost key appeared inside the lunch bag.

Use: at last or last in order

Cloze clue: Use for final step.

Example: Finally, revise the marked mistakes.

Use: after delay or difficulty

Cloze clue: Use when something happens after waiting.

Example: At last, the train arrived like a celebrity.

Use: immediately

Cloze clue: Use for instant action.

Example: The guard checked the alarm at once.

Use: immediately after

Cloze clue: Use with inversion when no sooner starts the sentence.

Example: No sooner did he sit down than the phone rang.

Use: almost immediately after

Cloze clue: Use with inversion when hardly starts the sentence.

Example: Hardly had she opened the book when the light went out.

Use: almost immediately after

Cloze clue: Use similar to hardly...when.

Example: Scarcely had he entered when everyone became silent.

Use: as soon as

Cloze clue: Use for immediate sequence.

Example: The moment the teacher entered, whispers disappeared.

Use: before or when a certain time arrives

Cloze clue: Use for deadline-like sequence.

Example: By the time he reached, the counter had closed.

Use: after something happens

Cloze clue: Use when one event enables the next.

Example: Once you understand the rule, the options look less scary.

Use: without being affected by

Cloze clue: Use before noun or pronoun.

Example: Regardless of difficulty, attempt the known questions first.

Use: however much

Cloze clue: Use before adjective or adverb.

Example: No matter how easy it looks, check the tense.

Use: whatever happens

Cloze clue: Use for strong concession.

Example: No matter what happens, do not leave OMR bubbles blank by accident.

Use: accepting that

Cloze clue: Use before an admitted point followed by contrast.

Example: Granted that the paper was tough, careless errors were still avoidable.

Use: it must be accepted that

Cloze clue: Use to admit a point before contrast.

Example: Admittedly, the rule is tricky. However, examples make it clear.

Use: even if that is true

Cloze clue: Use for formal concession before moving on.

Example: Be that as it may, the deadline will not change.

Use: as though

Cloze clue: Use for appearance or unreal comparison.

Example: He speaks as if he owns the entire library.

Use: as if

Cloze clue: Use for imaginary or apparent comparison.

Example: She looked as though she had solved the mystery.

Use: similar to

Cloze clue: Use before noun or pronoun in informal comparison.

Example: The room looked like a stationery shop after the exam.

Use: in exactly the same way

Cloze clue: Use for direct similarity.

Example: Just as muscles need practice, vocabulary needs repetition.

Use: similarly

Cloze clue: Use to compare method or effect.

Example: In the same way, daily reading improves cloze accuracy.

Use: to the same degree

Cloze clue: Use when two things have similar importance.

Example: Speed is important. Equally, accuracy decides selection.

Use: instead of

Cloze clue: Use to show preference between alternatives.

Example: Rather than guess wildly, eliminate wrong options.

Use: in comparison with

Cloze clue: Use for formal comparison.

Example: As compared with last year, the paper was easier.

Use: when compared

Cloze clue: Use to compare two ideas.

Example: In comparison, the second passage was clearer.

Use: examined against

Cloze clue: Use for direct comparison of differences.

Example: Compared with the first mock, his second score improved.

Use: used before an example

Cloze clue: Use when one specific case illustrates the point.

Example: Many words change meaning by context. For example, charge can mean accuse or ask money.

Use: for example

Cloze clue: Use to introduce one example.

Example: Some nouns are uncountable. For instance, advice does not take plural s.

Use: like or including

Cloze clue: Use before examples.

Example: Read newspapers such as The Hindu and Indian Express.

Use: specifically

Cloze clue: Use before exact names or details.

Example: Three topics need revision, namely articles, prepositions, and narration.

Use: in other words

Cloze clue: Use to clarify or restate.

Example: He is a teetotaller, that is, he does not drink alcohol.

Use: to say differently

Cloze clue: Use to simplify or restate.

Example: The sentence is passive. In other words, the object has become the subject.

Use: to give an example

Cloze clue: Use before a clarifying example.

Example: To illustrate, honest takes an because h is silent.

Use: in simple words

Cloze clue: Use before a simplified explanation.

Example: To put it simply, did takes the base verb.

Use: in exact detail

Cloze clue: Use when narrowing a broad idea.

Example: Specifically, the error is in the verb form.

Use: especially

Cloze clue: Use to highlight one item from a group.

Example: Grammar traps, in particular prepositions, need repeated practice.

Use: actually or more strongly

Cloze clue: Use to correct or strengthen an idea.

Example: The rule is not rare. In fact, it appears often.

Use: really or certainly

Cloze clue: Use for emphasis or confirmation.

Example: The question was tricky. Indeed, most students missed it.

Use: because we must remember

Cloze clue: Use to give a reason that supports a conclusion.

Example: Do not skip revision. After all, easy marks matter.

Use: finally, to sum up

Cloze clue: Use at the end of an argument or essay.

Example: In conclusion, accuracy beats blind speed.

Use: to end the discussion

Cloze clue: Use before final statement.

Example: To conclude, cloze tests reward context reading.

Use: briefly

Cloze clue: Use to summarise.

Example: In short, read before and after the blank.

Use: in a few words

Cloze clue: Use for concise summary.

Example: In brief, connectors show relationships.

Use: to summarise

Cloze clue: Use before final summary.

Example: To sum up, cause and result words are different.

Use: considering everything

Cloze clue: Use for overall judgment.

Example: On the whole, the passage was easy but the options were clever.

Use: considering everything

Cloze clue: Use for general conclusion.

Example: All in all, the mock test was a useful warning.

Use: generally

Cloze clue: Use for broad conclusion.

Example: Overall, her grammar improved after error analysis.

Use: finally in the end

Cloze clue: Use for final result after a process.

Example: Ultimately, consistency defeated fear.

Use: basically

Cloze clue: Use for core idea.

Example: In essence, a connector shows how ideas are linked.

Use: definitely

Cloze clue: Use when there is no doubt.

Example: Certainly, daily practice improves speed.

Use: certainly or I believe strongly

Cloze clue: Use for confident statement, sometimes emotional.

Example: Surely, one silly mistake is enough motivation to revise.

Use: without doubt

Cloze clue: Use for strong certainty.

Example: Undoubtedly, vocabulary helps in cloze tests.

Use: obviously

Cloze clue: Use when evidence is easy to see.

Example: Clearly, the answer cannot be but after because.

Use: clearly

Cloze clue: Use when something is easily understood.

Example: Obviously, no sooner needs than.

Use: most importantly

Cloze clue: Use to highlight the strongest point.

Example: Above all, read the whole sentence before choosing.

Use: particularly

Cloze clue: Use to single out something important.

Example: Prepositions are tricky, especially after adjectives.

Use: especially

Cloze clue: Use for special emphasis.

Example: This rule is useful, particularly in error spotting.

Use: above all

Cloze clue: Use for the key point.

Example: Most importantly, do not ignore the word after the blank.

Use: naturally or certainly

Cloze clue: Use for expected or accepted fact.

Example: Of course, context matters more than guessing.

Use: whatever happens

Cloze clue: Use to return to a main point.

Example: In any case, the form must be submitted today.

Use: minimum or positive side

Cloze clue: Use for minimum amount or consolation.

Example: The mock was hard. At least, it exposed weak areas.

Use: in reality

Cloze clue: Use to correct or clarify.

Example: Actually, advice is uncountable.

Use: if we are exact

Cloze clue: Use for precise correction.

Example: Strictly speaking, data is plural in formal grammar.

Use: excluding

Cloze clue: Use before the excluded person or thing.

Example: Everyone submitted the form except Ravi.

Use: apart from one problem

Cloze clue: Use to mention a small exception to a general statement.

Example: The essay was good except for spelling mistakes.

Use: except for or besides

Cloze clue: Use depending on context, exclusion or addition.

Example: Apart from one error, the answer was perfect.

Use: except for, formal

Cloze clue: Use for formal exception.

Example: Save for a few typos, the report was clean.

Use: except

Cloze clue: Use to exclude something.

Example: Other than grammar, his English was strong.

Use: except for

Cloze clue: Use before a possible exception.

Example: Barring rain, the match will start on time.

Use: without the help or effect of

Cloze clue: Use to show something would not happen without a factor.

Example: But for her guidance, he would have failed.

Use: on some occasions

Cloze clue: Use for occasional truth.

Example: Sometimes, the shortest option is the trap.

Use: many times

Cloze clue: Use for frequent events.

Example: Often, the clue lies after the blank.

Use: in most cases

Cloze clue: Use for general rule with exceptions.

Example: Usually, since takes a starting point.

Use: normally

Cloze clue: Use for broad statement.

Example: Generally, articles depend on sound.

Use: not often

Cloze clue: Use for uncommon events.

Example: Rarely does an error shout its own name.

Use: rarely

Cloze clue: Use formally for not often.

Example: Seldom do students forget a mistake that cost them marks.

Use: almost never

Cloze clue: Use for very rare frequency.

Example: He hardly ever guesses without eliminating options.

Use: sometimes

Cloze clue: Use for occasional events.

Example: Occasionally, a passage gives the answer in the next line.

Use: often

Cloze clue: Use for repeated events.

Example: Frequently, SSC tests fixed prepositions.

Use: sometimes

Cloze clue: Use for occasional situations.

Example: At times, even simple grammar feels slippery.

Use: maybe

Cloze clue: Use for uncertainty.

Example: Perhaps the answer is however, but check the contrast first.

Use: maybe

Cloze clue: Use for uncertain possibility.

Example: Possibly, the passage is hinting at a result.

Use: very likely

Cloze clue: Use when something is likely but not certain.

Example: Probably, the blank needs a cause connector.

Use: probably

Cloze clue: Use as adjective or adverb depending on structure.

Example: The result is likely to improve with practice.

Use: as it seems

Cloze clue: Use when something appears true based on evidence.

Example: Apparently, the easy option was the trap.

Use: probably based on assumption

Cloze clue: Use when making a reasonable guess.

Example: Presumably, he left early because the office was closed.

Use: it can be argued that

Cloze clue: Use for debatable claim.

Example: Arguably, connectors are easier than vocabulary if logic is clear.

Use: as stated by

Cloze clue: Use to cite a source or authority.

Example: According to the report, rainfall increased this year.

Use: according to a rule or agreement

Cloze clue: Use for compliance.

Example: The form was rejected in accordance with the rules.

Use: consistent with

Cloze clue: Use when something matches a rule or trend.

Example: The decision was in line with the guidelines.

Use: about

Cloze clue: Use to introduce topic.

Example: Regarding your application, the office needs one document.

Use: about

Cloze clue: Use for formal topic reference.

Example: Concerning the delay, the railway issued a notice.

Use: concerning

Cloze clue: Use for topic introduction.

Example: As regards grammar, repeated practice is necessary.

Use: with respect to

Cloze clue: Use to discuss one aspect.

Example: In terms of accuracy, she improved greatly.

Use: concerning

Cloze clue: Use for formal topic reference.

Example: With regard to fees, the notice is clear.

Use: speaking about

Cloze clue: Use to shift focus to a topic.

Example: As for vocabulary, daily revision is enough.

Use: in this matter

Cloze clue: Use to refer to a particular aspect.

Example: In this respect, the second plan is better.

Use: in this situation

Cloze clue: Use to link to current discussion.

Example: In this context, however is the correct connector.

Use: referring to

Cloze clue: Use in formal communication.

Example: With reference to your letter, the office replied.

Use: related to

Cloze clue: Use for formal relation.

Example: He was questioned in connection with the case.

Use: about or concerning

Cloze clue: Use in formal discussion.

Example: There was doubt as to his eligibility.
